issues.description: Only original Wellcome 1647 English witness checked; no upstream authorial manuscript or corrected 1659 edition collated.

The original chart glyph ♃ and 8 Maij are visible. Thursday8 May1645 Julian is an inference from the English 1645 calendar and weekday; not a printed calendar designation. Earlier May24 was a transcription error, explicitly superseded.
Printed 6:15 P.M and hor: astr do not license a modern local civil timezone or UTC timestamp; London or any chart locality is not supplied in this case caption.
The case diagram is preserved in original pixels; full planetary degrees, glyphs, houses and aspects not independently transcribed or ephemeris-parity checked.
Chele / Chelae fixed star reference not securely identified or mapped to a modern catalogue.
The sign/house interpretation of Scorpio, Saturn in sixth, Aries and Mars in Leo is historical source logic not anatomy or verified medical diagnosis.
Mars was in Cancer AT EARLIER square with Saturn; author also locates it in Leo for present-heart testimony. Keep distinct time contexts and source degree precision unresolved.
Saturn and Mars planetary terms, lunar house, dexter square, sextile and antiscion lack exact reproducible modern algorithm/orb for this chart.

Source back-references in this case: head/Aries page245, Saturn in Aries breast page113, sixth/body and Saturn infirmities page244 twice, and Saturn duration page248. Mars in Leo heart line has no explicit separate page citation. Earlier pages were not independently re-read in this chapter.
Historical melancholy, dry disease, choler, obstruction, consumption, jaundice and red gravel wording cannot be translated automatically into modern medical diagnoses.
The author spoke to the doctor and describes symptoms; chart creation/interpretation timing relative to symptom disclosure is not established by this narrative.
One chart, one patient, one retrospective author-reported death; repeated observations and testimonies have zero independent-case multiplicity.
The claimed death on August14 following is not an independently authenticated outcome and no prospectively frozen source rule is shown.
The author's gently hot/moist/cordial drug advice is 17th-century historical text, not modern safe or effective treatment.
Original source ☽ in ♒ (Moon Aquarius) glyph is readable in PDF322, but the asserted Secrets/bladder medical correspondence is only old doctrine, not independently validated anatomy.
Fixed angles, fixed luminaries, antiscion, terms and prior aspects may be dependent testimonies, not additive independent probabilities.
The text gives neither a clinical denominator nor negative case controls, and demonstrates no prospective astrological predictive validity.
Printed end-of-case divider at PDF322 and Chapter XLVI heading at PDF323 separate this dated 1645 doctor from the next medical patient.
Lilly prints reported death 14 August BEFORE his following written long/short illness explanation; retrospective fit and chart-age arithmetic are not evidence of a prospective frozen forecast.
The meaning of source hor: astr: and the chart center sequence with Latin ad/et remain undecided without independent glyph collation.
Chart center ♀ ☽ a △ ☿ / ad □ ☉ / et ✶ ♄: attachment of ♀, literal Latin a/ad/et and some glyphs uncertain; full degree transcription remains open.
Moon out of his Termes: both “out of” as outside versus from, and “his” Saturn versus Mars remain ambiguous, so no negative lunar dignity predicate is implemented.
Moon and Sun “out of Angles”: early modern usage ambiguous and possibly at odds with Moon in fourth and planet diagram locations; no automatic not-angular test.
The author printed a duration rationale after saying the doctor died; ordering prevents using that paragraph as demonstrably prospective prediction.
Marginal handwriting on PDF321 near the page header (“6th House”) and beside printed page113 (approximately “119+”) is copy-specific, unauthenticated and not an authorial erratum.
PDF323 following Chapter XLVI boundary was visually inspected by controller, but first independent reviewer could not locate that boundary image; do not misstate as independently re-read.

Chart wheel degree/cusp locations not completely independently transcribed or validated: a high-resolution image and partial observations are retained with uncertainty rather than forcing a modern horoscope.
